title: Derived extension of scalars is left adjoint to termwise restriction
statement:
In the situation of [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-kflat], there is an adjunction
$$
\mathcal S\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\mathcal R}-\dashv D(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)
$$
between the derived extension of scalars and the termwise restriction of scalars.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$, $U=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$, $F=LE$ and $G=RU$. The ambient hypotheses in [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-kflat] are precisely those of [def-sfb-derived-extend-restrict-adjunction]: a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions, and a morphism of commutative ring objects. The latter node therefore supplies $F\dashv G$, with natural bijections $a_{K,N}:\operatorname{Hom}(FK,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(K,GN)$ for $K\in D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$, $N\in D(\Mod_{\mathcal S})$. By definition $F=\mathcal S\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\mathcal R}-$; no flatness of $\mathcal S$ as an $\mathcal R$-module or boundedness of complexes is imposed.

source.place: only paragraph: the derived adjunction to be transported

proof.text: Under the same hypotheses, [def-sfb-derived-restrict-levelwise] supplies a canonical natural isomorphism $\rho:G\xrightarrow{\sim}H$, where $H=D(U):D(\Mod_{\mathcal S})\to D(\Mod_{\mathcal R})$ is restriction applied termwise. Both $G$ and $H$ have this direction, so each $\rho_N$ can be postcomposed with a map $K\to GN$.

source.place: only paragraph: canonical isomorphism of the two right adjoints

proof.text:
Define $b_{K,N}(h)=\rho_N\circ a_{K,N}(h)$. Its inverse is $c_{K,N}(k)=a_{K,N}^{-1}(\rho_N^{-1}\circ k)$. The identities $\rho_N^{-1}\rho_N=1$ and $\rho_N\rho_N^{-1}=1$ give $cb(h)=h$ and $bc(k)=k$. For $u:K'\to K$ and $v:N\to N'$, naturality of $a$ and $\rho$ gives explicitly
$$b_{K',N'}(v\circ h\circ F(u))=\rho_{N'}\circ G(v)\circ a_{K,N}(h)\circ u
=H(v)\circ b_{K,N}(h)\circ u.$$
Thus $b$ is a natural Hom bijection and defines the required adjunction $F\dashv H$. Its unit is $\rho_{FK}\circ\eta_K$ and its counit at $N$ is $\epsilon_N\circ F(\rho_N^{-1})$, where $\eta,\epsilon$ belong to the adjunction in step 1. This is the transport of that adjunction along exactly the canonical isomorphism in step 2. The inverse and naturality computations give the construction directly, without a separate transport lemma.

proof_origin.place: only paragraph, expanded by the explicit natural Hom bijection
